text:
rachael: Noticed a weird pattern: ap-central has ~120 tiny GPU fragments (2-4 GB) scattered across nodes, scheduler keeps evicting small latency-sensitive pods to coalesce for reserved hires. Queue jitter reported by infra-team jobs.
diego: yep saw the same. It's the mixed GPU memory flavors again; packer prefers to create large contiguous regions for p4-like reserved jobs. Tiny pods bounce.
min: past fixes (warmpool bump, tolerations) helped but we keep seeing a slow steady-state churn during nightly rollout window.
rachael: idea: add a short-lived "fragment-shepherd" admission hint. When a pod is small (<4GB) and namespace=nonprod, scheduler will prefer to land it on nodes labeled fragment-friendly (warm-pool or low-util nodes). This avoids global repack.
diego: operationally: label a small set of nodes per AZ as fragment-friendly and add a scoring bonus. We can canary to one AZ.
min: runbook: 1) label nodes 2) add scoring +40 for label fragment-friendly 3) patch low-prio ns tolerations to accept landing there. Duration 45m.
ops: infra-bot: creating runbook entry for fragment-shepherd canary in ap-central-1a. owner=rachael, id=r-frag-01.
rachael: commands I'll run (dry-run first):
```bash
# label 6 nodes in ap-central-1a
kubectl label node gpu-node-0{1..6} fragment-friendly=true
# canary scoring configmap (apply to 10% schedulers)
kubectl -n kube-system apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-scheduler-config
data:
  fragmentShepherdScore: "40"
  cohort: "ap-central-frag-canary"
EOF
```
diego: i'll prepare toleration patch for spot-ns and batch-dev: apply tolerationSeconds=1800 so they can land without touching customer nodes.
min: warm-pool unchanged for this experiment, we're relying on fragment-friendly labels to absorb.
infra-bot: [info] canary prechecks passed. dry-run scheduler apply OK.
rachael: applying labels now to 6 nodes.
infra-bot: [info] nodes labeled: gpu-node-01..gpu-node-06.
diego: applying namespace tolerations now.
infra-bot: [info] namespace tolerations patched for spot-ns and batch-dev.
rachael: canary apply of configmap to 10% schedulers in ap-central-1a.
infra-bot: [metric] immediate telemetry: fit_failures down -8% (5m), preempt_rate down -10%. pod_start_p50 improved ~30s.
min: promising. Any negative effect on reserved tail latency?
diego: short-window looks fine; reserved-job p99 in canary az unchanged (+2% noise).
rachael: keep for 45m. If improvement holds, we'll expand to ap-central-1b and write RFC for fragment-shepherd as a permanent heuristic with thresholds.
min: follow-ups: 1) collect allocation traces (rachael) 2) cost estimate for running labeled nodes long-term (diego) 3) test interplay with eagerRepack flag (min).
infra-bot: [alert] runbook r-frag-01 active: will auto-expire in 45m unless extended.
rachael: thumbs up. If any regression, I'll rollback labels and configmap.
ops: noted. Logging this as ACIT (allocation-capture-id) for post-analysis.
